newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares close lower on foreign selling.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares close lower on foreign selling.

text.p: Manila shares edged down on Tuesday as foreign funds continued to pocket their gains to realign their portfolio in the region, traders said.
The main index shaved off 8.43 points to close at 2,927.43 points following Monday's 37.27-point fall.
"Technically, the market is still weak. A lot of foreigners are cashing in on hefty gains," said Peter Mutuc, managing director of HG Asia Securities.
"The market is still up by 13 percent from the start of the year," Mutuc pointed out.
Fundamentally, he said there was no reason to sell down the Philippines because of the country's good economic fundamentals.
Ramon Lucas, research manager of Rashid Hussain Securities, said no one would move aggressively into the market until foreign funds start returning.
"We're just waiting for traces of any significant moves from foreign investors," he said.
Mutuc, however, believed the market should hold for awhile, with support seen at 2,920 to 2,900 points.
Among the index stocks, Manila Electric Co B shares gave up 4.0 pesos to 174 pesos.

However, Ayala Land Inc B shares bounced back by 50 centavos to close at 26.50 after reaching its support level at 26 pesos, dealers said. Ayala Land had suffered from profit-taking on concerns the country's real estate market would soon cool down.

San Miguel Corp B shares rose 50 centavos to close at 87 pesos on expectations the food and beer company's earnings would move up substantially in the fourth quarter with the recovery of the farm sector, analysts said.
